en: **The Hymn to Umā-Maheśvara** Composed by Śrī Śaṅkarācārya Salutations to Śiva and Śivā, who possess ever-new youth, whose bodies are entwined with one another, who have the daughter of the lord of serpents and the bull as their emblems; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī. Salutations to Śiva and Śivā, who delight in the festival of love, who grant the desired boons to those who bow before them, and whose sandals are worshipped by Nārāyaṇa; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī.

Salutations to Śiva and Śivā, who ride upon the bull, who are well-worshipped by Viriñci, Viṣṇu, and Indra, and who are anointed with sacred ashes and sandalwood paste; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī. (3) Salutations to Śiva and Śivā, the lords of the universe, the masters of the world, whose forms are ever-victorious, and who are saluted by the foremost of gods headed by Indra; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī. (4) Salutations to Śiva and Śivā, who are the supreme medicine, and who are adorned within the cage of the five-syllabled mantra.

Salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī, who perform the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the phenomenal world. || 5 || Salutations to the auspicious pair, most beautiful, whose lotus-hearts are intensely attached to one another; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī, the sole benefactors of the welfare of all the worlds. || 6 || Salutations to the auspicious pair, the destroyers of the Kali age, who bear bodies as auspicious as skeletons; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī, the deities residing on Mount Kailāsa. || 7 ||

Salutations to Śiva and Śivā, who remove all inauspiciousness, who are uniquely exalted as the sole lords of the entire world, who are unimpeded, and who are the source of all memory; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī. (8) Salutations to Śiva and Śivā, whose vehicle is the chariot, whose eyes are the sun, the moon, and fire, and whose lotus-face possesses the luster of the full moon; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī. (9) Salutations to Śiva and Śivā, who wear matted hair, and who are entirely free from old age and death.

Salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī, who are worshipped by Janārdana and the one born from the lotus (Brahmā). Salutations to the auspicious Śiva and Śivā, the three-eyed ones, who bear bilva leaves and garlands of jasmine; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī, the lords of Śobhāvatī and Śāntavatī. Salutations to the auspicious Śiva and Śivā, the protectors of creatures whose hearts are fixed on guarding the three worlds; salutations again and again to Śaṅkara and Pārvatī, who are worshipped by all the gods and asuras.

The man who recites this hymn of twelve verses with devotion to Śiva and Pārvatī at the three junctions of the day enjoys the fruits of all good fortune; at the end of his life, he attains the world of Śiva and lives for a hundred years. Thus ends the Umāmaheśvara Stotra.
